294 N = 60 kg x 9.81 x 0.5 uses the limit mass, not 46 kg robot (+15 kg soil gives 299 N, so effect small).

C1.why: Mass is summed (46 kg vs 60 kg) but the stowed 0.90x0.42x0.45 m box is only claimed; the drawn ladder rises far above 0.45 m and no folding of the ladder is described (major).

C2.why: Kerf chain plus bucket ladder plus screw pour is a plausible chain, but as drawn the ladder foot is on top of the chassis away from the chain, so loosened soil has no path into the buckets (major).

C3.why: Mass, sag and pressure re-derive, but ladder power uses the full-width 32.9 N not the 11 N kerf force, traction uses 60 kg not the robot mass, stop distance 0.308 m contradicts its own 0.56 m table; key numbers are pasted code fragments.

C4.why: Picture shows one wheel, a front end held up by the trenching chain, a ladder that does not reach the trench, and an untilted hopper whose screw points past the bin.

C5.why: Risks named honestly (arching, blind tip), but the box claim and the soil path are not shown to close.

C6.why: Step list explains the soil route in words, but the text 'wide ladder lifts side spoil' is unclear about how kerf spoil reaches the buckets.

C7.why: Five ordered build steps with materials and sizes, illustrated; adequate but thin on the ladder fold and tilt mechanism.

C8.why: Missing front/side wheels (one wheel visible on a four-wheel machine) and a chassis floating on the chain are generator mistakes.

Claimed 273 N twin draft at 5 kPa, but the shown calc prints 33.2 N.

C2.why: RASSOR-type counter-rotating drums are proven in BP-1, but as drawn both drums are stacked on one forward arm so only one can touch the ground (major).

C7.why: Four ordered steps with materials, sizes and reasons, each illustrated.

faults.fault: Rotor drawn with four blades in panels A and B; text: three-blade rotor.
Using the 38.1 mm post as scale, hub to generator end spans ~0.49 m, over the 45 cm cube and the stated 36 cm stack; rotor appears ~0.33 m not 0.40 m.
8.41 V at 1430 rpm is open-circuit (1430/170); after a Schottky bridge (~0.5-1 V) and winding drop under load it is below the 8 V regulator minimum, so the 2.08 W at 5 m/s is not shown.
Thrust is checked (Ct = 1, conservative) but the fixed-pitch rotor's free-running speed and blade centrifugal stress for 3D-printed blades at 22 m/s are not computed; 'soft stall' asserted.
I = 1.5e-8 m^4 used; a 38.1 x 3.18 mm tube has 5.36e-8 m^4, so stress 16.6 MPa is overstated ~3.6x (safe side).
Part named 'Steel post clamp and post' but post is 6061-T6 aluminium.
'Spring-applied disc brake' leader points at generator end; disc is item 6.
85.6 W at 18.5 V open-circuit into 4 ohm exceeds ~26 W rotor input; winding resistance ignored.

C1.why: 40 cm rotor with 2.5 cm side clearance and shutdown with spring brake are computed; production at 5 m/s rests on an open-circuit 8.41 V that falls below the 8 V regulator floor after bridge/winding drops (major).

C2.why: Fixed-pitch rotor, outrunner and fail-safe spring disc plus dump is a sound concept; low-wind electrical chain and free-running survival at 22 m/s are not closed (major).

C3.why: Wind power, rpm, Kv volts, thrust, deflection, KE and disc rise re-derive; post I is 1.5e-8 vs 5.4e-8 for the stated tube (conservative), and the 5 m/s voltage is open-circuit.

C4.why: Picture shows four blades and a ~0.5 m hub-to-generator shaft (scaled by the 38 mm post), contradicting three blades and the 36 cm stack.

C5.why: Risks name the dump-only runaway and the Kv choice, and both are addressed.

C6.why: Clear chain from wind to load and the trip logic for command and disconnect.

C7.why: Four steps with materials; only two illustrated; blade making only '3D-printed'.

C8.why: Four-blade rotor on a 'three-blade' design is a generator count error; label 'spring-applied disc brake' points at the generator end.

faults.fault: Four blades drawn; text: 3x carbon blades.
E-stop/dump-resistor enclosure mounted on the post below the nacelle, outside the cube; only the post may be outside.
25 cm nacelle + 18 cm tail = 43 cm leaves 2 cm for rotor hub depth and pitch slider; 'fits with 2 cm clearance' not supported.
'>4x margin' for shaft and blades at 22 m/s given without stress calc; servo torque against centrifugal twisting at up to 6000 rpm not computed.
Uncontrolled 6300 rpm at 22 m/s; at TSR 5.5 it is 5780 rpm.
2-3 s from 59 J / >25 W ignores falling short-circuit torque at low speed; plausible but not computed.
Servo 'holds feather without power draw' vs supercap powering it.
Only 85% generator efficiency applied; rectifier and MPPT losses omitted.

C2.why: Pitch-to-feather plus generator short with spring return is a robust, well-known way to limit and stop; works in principle.

C3.why: Swept power, rpm, thrust and KE re-derive; '>4x margin' structure, servo authority and stop time are asserted not computed; 6300 rpm vs 5780 at TSR 5.5.

C4.why: Picture shows the pitch hub and tail vane as described, but four blades against three and an electronics box on the post.

C5.why: Risks (pitch jam, resistor heat, flutter, false trip) are real and mitigated.

C6.why: Clear explanation of normal running, power limiting and the shutdown sequence.

C7.why: Specific make steps for blades, mechanics, electrics and test.

C8.why: Four-blade rotor is a generator count error; 'DUMP RESISTOR' text legible.

Four modules drawn; text: 6 x 400 W. Six modules (11.2 m^2) also exceed the 5.8 m^2 roof footprint, not addressed.
25.6 m^2 vs 24.4 m^2 internal and 33.2 m^2 external for the stated dimensions.
5.27 kWh/2.11 kWh in one place, 5.65/2.26 kWh in the constraint check.
'1.8 days' is 3.84/2.11 transmission-only; with full 3.56 kWh/day holding it is ~1.1 day.
Chamber drawn with no front wall; eight crates shown vs twenty.

faults.fault: 200-300 kg ice x 334 kJ/kg = 18.6-27.8 kWh thermal per day to freeze; at freezing COP ~2 this is ~10 kWh electric not in the 7-9 kWh/day budget.
2.5 kWp x 4-5 h = 10-12.5 kWh with no system losses; with 0.75 derate 7.5-9.4 kWh, at or below the stated load.
Envelope transmission (about 200 W for 26.3 m^2 at U 0.2, 38 K) never computed; loads scaled from precedents.
Box drawn with a machine bay holding chiller, battery and tanks plus a cold compartment about half the width; text describes one 2.4x1.8x2.1 m cold room.
Cold-air arrows go from the evaporator in the machine bay across the partition and spill out of the open door onto the floor.
'658W/h' is not a unit of power or energy.
Ice-bank tanks drawn as pressurised gas cylinders.

C1.why: Solar-only and 1 t claimed MET by precedent (ColdHubs, 4.85 m^3 store), not by its own energy balance (major).

C2.why: Vapour compression plus ice bank plus battery is a valid concept, but freezing 200-300 kg of ice daily (~23 kWh thermal) is not in the 7-9 kWh electric budget and PV yield is overstated (no losses applied) (major).

C3.why: Transmission load never computed; PV 10-12.5 kWh/day has no system derate (7.5-9.4 kWh with 0.75); room volume 9.1 m^3 stated ~7; '658 W/h' unit garble.

C4.why: Picture splits the box into a machine bay and a narrow cold compartment roughly half the width, unlike the 2.4x1.8 m room; cold-air arrows cross the partition and pour out of the open door.

C5.why: Risks are honest and practical (cloudy days, warm loading, R290 servicing).

C6.why: How it works is clear and plain.

C7.why: Four make steps with processes, few dimensions, no illustrations.

C8.why: Airflow arrows passing through walls and out the door; tanks drawn as pressure cylinders rather than ice-bank tanks.

C3.why: Envelope, conduction, thermal total, electrical load, yield, mass, pad pressure, uplift and anchors all re-derive; door infiltration assumes only 1 m^3 per opening (full change ~0.88 kWh/day, within margin).

C4.why: Picture shows split array, pads, frame and monoblock, but only five ground modules vs seven and label 5 ('insulated chamber') points at the cooler while the cooler is 'not located'.
